2.text: The herdsmen, of course, never count their reindeer, nor are they able

3.text: to remember all their animals by their looks, as has been asserted by travellers.¹

4.text: In the larger herds they know only the more conspicuous animals, such as

5.text: breeding-bucks, old dams, harness-animals, etc. If there be any loss, they

6.text: become aware of it only by the absence of one of them. Of the smaller

7.text: animals they take little notice, nor do they care much about them.

8.text: The Rev. Argentoff relates that one Maiˊñɪ-qlaˊul, a rich reindeer-breeder

9.text: from the Dry Anui, tried to ascertain the number of his animals by counting

10.text: them by corrals. Each corralful was represented by a chip of wood, and these

11.text: were placed together in a glove.² Operations of this kind were performed

12.text: by the rich Tungus for the same purpose; but among the Chukchee they can

13.text: occur only exceptionally, because every new experiment with the herd is

14.text: considered to thwart the qaˊa-vaˊɪrg̣ɪn (literally, “reindeer substance;” i. e., the

16.text: Seasons. — It may not be out of place to add here the Chukchee method

17.text: of dividing the year. The year is divided into twelve lunar months or “moons”

18.text: (yiˊᵋlhɪn). The series begins with the winter solstice, the time of which is

19.text: marked pretty accurately. The dark interval between two “moons” is called

20.text: “moon interval” (yuˊᵋtir). The names of the months are —

21.text: 1. ɪnp-luˊwleñ-yiˊᵋlhɪn (“old-buck month”), from about the 20th of December to the 20th of January.

22.text: The origin of the name is uncertain.

31.text: 10. G̣ɪthaˊ-êˊᵋlhɪn (“autumn month”), called also ɪlv-eiˊñe-yiˊᵋlhɪn (“wild-reindeer rutting month”).

32.text: 11. Yaraˊučɪn, probably from Yaˊraw (“muscles of the back”), because it is supposed that the

33.text: muscles of a reindeer’s back strengthen in mid-winter. The same name, with the same expla-

34.text: nation, was found among the Koryak of the western shore of Kamchatka in the form

35.text: yaraˊwučɪn. This month is also called by the Chukchee Tuˊr-eᵋče (“new-snow cover”).

37.text: The Maritime Chukchee use the same table of months. The Koryak in

38.text: different localities have different systems of names, but for the third and the

39.text: fourth month most of them have names signifying “false reindeer-birth month”

40.text: and “genuine reindeer-birth month.” ³ Of course, the twelve lunar months do

41.text: not exactly coincide with the solar year between two winter solstices; but the

42.text: Chukchee do not care about a few extra days. In ordinary talk the names

43.text: of the months are often replaced by those of the seasons, which are much more

44.text: numerous than with us. The following are most frequently employed.
